body:
# Ticket 1 — Remember, list and forget Claude accounts — Round 1

### Blocked by
—

### Description
T3 can remember the Claude account that is currently logged in on one of its Claude setups, under a name the user chooses, show which accounts it remembers and which account is active on each Claude setup, and forget a remembered account again. Several accounts can be remembered per machine. The remembered login is kept in T3's own secret storage with the same protection as T3's other secrets and never appears in a listing, an error, or a log. Forgetting never touches a setup: an account that is still logged in stays logged in.

This ticket builds the backend service only. Nothing calls it from a client yet (a later frontend Auftrag does that), and switching between accounts is ticket 2 and ticket 3. On any system other than Linux, all three actions answer that they are unavailable.

A "Claude setup" is a configured Claude provider instance (driver kind `claudeAgent`), addressed by its `ProviderInstanceId`.

### Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario AK-1: Remember the account logged in on a setup under a chosen name
  Given a Claude setup on which the account "alice@example.com" is logged in
  And T3 remembers no accounts yet
  When T3 is asked to remember this setup's account under the name "Work"
  Then T3 remembers one account named "Work" for "alice@example.com"
Serves: R1

Scenario AK-2: Several accounts can be remembered on one machine
  Given T3 remembers the account "alice@example.com" under the name "Work"
  And a second Claude setup on which "bob@example.com" is logged in
  When T3 is asked to remember the second setup's account under the name "Private"
  Then T3 remembers both "Work" and "Private"
Serves: R1

Scenario AK-3: Remembering is refused when no account is logged in
  Given a Claude setup on which no account is logged in
  When T3 is asked to remember this setup's account under the name "Work"
  Then the request is refused with the reason that no account is logged in on this setup
  And T3 remembers no new account
Serves: R1

Scenario AK-4: Remembering under a name already in use is refused
  Given T3 remembers "alice@example.com" under the name "Work"
  And a Claude setup on which "bob@example.com" is logged in
  When T3 is asked to remember this setup's account under the name "Work"
  Then the request is refused with the reason that the name "Work" is already in use
  And "Work" still stands for "alice@example.com"
Serves: R1

Scenario AK-5: List shows remembered accounts and the active account per setup
  Given T3 remembers "Work" for "alice@example.com" and "Private" for "bob@example.com"
  And setup one has "alice@example.com" logged in and setup two has "bob@example.com" logged in
  When T3 is asked which accounts it remembers
  Then the answer names "Work" and "Private"
  And it shows "Work" as active on setup one and "Private" as active on setup two
Serves: R2

Scenario AK-6: List shows an active account that is not remembered
  Given a Claude setup on which "carol@example.com" is logged in
  And T3 does not remember "carol@example.com"
  When T3 is asked which accounts it remembers
  Then the answer shows "carol@example.com" as active on that setup
  And it marks that account as not remembered
Serves: R2

Scenario AK-7: List with nothing remembered
  Given T3 remembers no accounts
  When T3 is asked which accounts it remembers
  Then the answer contains no remembered accounts
  And it still shows which account is active on each Claude setup
Serves: R2

Scenario AK-8: Forget an account that is not active
  Given T3 remembers "Work" and "Private"
  And no Claude setup has the "Private" account active
  When T3 is asked to forget "Private"
  Then T3 remembers only "Work"
Serves: R3

Scenario AK-9: Forgetting the active account keeps the setup logged in
  Given a Claude setup with "alice@example.com" logged in, remembered as "Work"
  When T3 is asked to forget "Work"
  Then T3 no longer remembers "Work"
  And the setup is still logged in as "alice@example.com"
  And a new turn in a thread on that setup runs as "alice@example.com"
Serves: R3

Scenario AK-23: Remembered logins are kept in T3's protected secret storage
  Given a Claude setup with "alice@example.com" logged in
  When T3 is asked to remember this setup's account under the name "Work"
  Then the saved login is kept with the same protection as T3's other secrets
  And it cannot be found in plain form anywhere else in T3's own data
Serves: R11

Scenario AK-24: The account list never reveals a login
  Given T3 remembers "Work" and "Private"
  When T3 is asked which accounts it remembers
  Then the answer contains names, account identities and which one is active
  And it contains no part of any saved login
Serves: R11

Scenario AK-27: Remembering is unavailable outside Linux
  Given a T3 server running on a system other than Linux
  When T3 is asked to remember a setup's account
  Then the answer says the action is unavailable on this system
  And nothing is remembered
Serves: R13

Scenario AK-28: Listing is unavailable outside Linux
  Given a T3 server running on a system other than Linux
  When T3 is asked which accounts it remembers
  Then the answer says the action is unavailable on this system
Serves: R13

Scenario AK-29: Forgetting is unavailable outside Linux
  Given a T3 server running on a system other than Linux
  When T3 is asked to forget a remembered account
  Then the answer says the action is unavailable on this system
Serves: R13
```

### Test specification
All tests use setups whose Claude config directory is a temporary directory the test creates and removes; no test reads or writes `~/.claude`, `~/.claude.json` or `~/.t3` (guard rail). Each setup is declared through `ServerSettingsService.layerTest({ providerInstances: { <id>: { driver: "claudeAgent", config: { homePath: <tmp dir> } } } })`, and its login is written by the test as two fixture files: `<tmp>/.credentials.json` = `{ "claudeAiOauth": { "accessToken": "<unique token>", "refreshToken": "<unique token>", "expiresAt": <ms>, "scopes": ["user:inference"] }, "mcpOAuth": { … } }` and `<tmp>/.claude.json` = `{ "oauthAccount": { "emailAddress": "alice@example.com", "accountUuid": "<uuid>", "organizationUuid": "<uuid>" }, "numStartups": 3, "projects": { … } }`. Token fixture values are unique random strings so a leak search cannot match by accident.

Unit (`apps/server/src/provider/Drivers/ClaudeHome.test.ts`, extended):
- `resolveClaudeSetupPaths` with a configured `homePath` returns that directory and `<dir>/.claude.json`.
- With an empty `homePath` and an inherited `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, it returns the inherited directory and `<inherited>/.claude.json`.
- With an empty `homePath` and no inherited `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, it returns `<home>/.claude` and `<home>/.claude.json` (with `HostProcess.HomeDirectory` provided as a temp path; nothing is read from disk).

Integration (`apps/server/src/provider/ClaudeAccounts.integration.test.ts`, through the `ClaudeAccounts` service, real `ServerSecretStore` over `ServerConfig.layerTest(process.cwd(), { prefix: "t3-claude-accounts-test-" })`, real `FileSystem`/`Path`, `HostProcess.Platform` provided as `"linux"` unless stated):
- AK-1: remember `{ instanceId: setupOne, name: "Work" }` on a logged-in setup returns `{ name: "Work", email: "alice@example.com" }`, and `list` then has exactly one account `{ name: "Work", email: "alice@example.com" }`.
- AK-2: after remembering two setups as "Work" and "Private", `list.accounts` is both, in that order.
- AK-3: a setup with no `.credentials.json` (and a second case: `.credentials.json` without `claudeAiOauth`) is refused with `ClaudeAccountError` reason `notLoggedIn`; `list.accounts` is unchanged.
- AK-4: remembering bob's setup as "Work" (and as " work ") is refused with reason `nameInUse`; `list.accounts` still holds exactly `{ name: "Work", email: "alice@example.com" }`.
- Remembering the same account (same `accountUuid` and `organizationUuid`) a second time under another name is refused with reason `alreadyRemembered`, naming the existing name.
- AK-5: two setups, two remembered accounts: `list.setups` shows setup one `active: { email: "alice@example.com", rememberedAs: "Work" }` and setup two `active: { email: "bob@example.com", rememberedAs: "Private" }`.
- AK-6: a setup with carol logged in and nothing remembered for carol shows `active: { email: "carol@example.com", rememberedAs: null }`.
- AK-7: with nothing remembered, `list.accounts` is `[]` and every configured Claude setup is still listed with its active account; a setup with nobody logged in is listed with `active: null`; a non-Claude instance (e.g. `driver: "codex"`) is not listed.
- AK-8: forget "Private" leaves `list.accounts` = `[Work]`.
- AK-9: forget "Work" while alice is logged in on setup one: `list.accounts` is `[]`, and both `<tmp>/.credentials.json` and `<tmp>/.claude.json` are byte-identical to before the call; `list.setups` still shows alice active with `rememberedAs: null`.
- Forgetting a name that is not remembered is refused with reason `accountNotFound`.
- AK-23: after remember, the secret `claude-accounts` exists in `<stateDir>/secrets/claude-accounts.bin` with file mode `0o600` in a `0o700` directory (same as every other T3 secret); a recursive walk of the whole temporary T3 base directory finds the fixture access token and refresh token in no file other than `claude-accounts.bin`.
- AK-24: `JSON.stringify(list)` contains neither fixture token, nor the substrings `accessToken`, `refreshToken`, `claudeAiOauth`; the listed account objects have exactly the keys `name` and `email`.
- No error raised by the service carries login content: for every refusal above, `JSON.stringify(error)` and `error.message` contain no fixture token.
- AK-27/AK-28/AK-29: with `HostProcess.Platform` provided as `"darwin"` (and once as `"win32"`), `remember`, `list` and `forget` each fail with reason `unavailable` and message "Claude account switching is unavailable on this system. It is supported on Linux only."; after the failed `remember`, `<stateDir>/secrets/claude-accounts.bin` does not exist.
Boundaries doubled: `HostProcess.Platform` and `HostProcess.HomeDirectory` (host OS), and the setup files (fixture files in temp dirs standing in for what the Claude CLI writes); everything else real — `ServerSecretStore`, `ServerSettingsService.layerTest`, `FileSystem`, `Path`.
e2e:
- There is no e2e suite (guard rail). AK-9's last line ("a new turn … runs as alice@example.com") needs a real Claude CLI; it is proven at the lowest level that can prove it: the setup's two login files are byte-identical after forgetting, so the next turn reads the same login. Named as such in the hand-off.

### Design reference


### Implementation details
Module: `apps/server` (provider)
Files:
- [MODIFY] `apps/server/src/provider/Drivers/ClaudeHome.ts` — add `resolveClaudeSetupPaths`, the one place that knows where a setup keeps its login and its account file.
- [MODIFY] `apps/server/src/provider/Drivers/ClaudeHome.test.ts` — unit tests for `resolveClaudeSetupPaths`.
- [MODIFY] `apps/server/src/provider/Drivers/ClaudeDriver.ts` — replace the inline `configDir`/`accountConfigPath` computation (lines 158–163) with `resolveClaudeSetupPaths(effectiveConfig, processEnv)`; behaviour unchanged.
- [MODIFY] `apps/server/src/provider/claudeResetCredits.ts` — delete the `claudeAccountConfigPath` export, whose only importer was ClaudeDriver (Knip fails CI on an unused export).
- [NEW] `apps/server/src/provider/claudeLoginFiles.ts` — read a setup's current Claude login and account identity from its two files.
- [NEW] `apps/server/src/provider/ClaudeAccounts.ts` — the `ClaudeAccounts` service: remember, list, forget, Linux gate, storage in `ServerSecretStore`.
- [NEW] `apps/server/src/provider/ClaudeAccounts.integration.test.ts` — the integration tests above.
- [MODIFY] `apps/server/src/server.ts` — add `ClaudeAccounts.layer` to the `Layer.mergeAll(...)` list of `layerRuntimeCoreDependenciesBase` next to `ProviderUsageLimitsIngestion.layer` (server.ts:601), where `layerServerSettings` and `ServerSecretStore.layer` are provided below it.

Consumes: nothing from earlier tickets. Existing: `ServerSecretStore.ServerSecretStore` (`get`, `set`), `ServerSettingsService` (`getSettings`), `deriveProviderInstanceConfigMap` (ProviderInstanceRegistryHydration.ts), `ClaudeSettings` (`@t3tools/contracts`), `mergeProviderInstanceEnvironment` (`@t3tools/provider-core/server/instanceEnvironment`), `resolveClaudeHomePath`, `HostProcess.Platform`, `HostProcess.HomeDirectory`.

Produces (names used letter for letter by tickets 2 and 3):
- In `ClaudeHome.ts`:
  ```ts
  export interface ClaudeSetupPaths {
    readonly configDir: string;          // holds .credentials.json
    readonly accountConfigPath: string;  // the .claude.json holding oauthAccount
  }
  export const resolveClaudeSetupPaths: (
    config: Pick<ClaudeSettings, "homePath">,
    environment?: NodeJS.ProcessEnv,
  ) => Effect.Effect<ClaudeSetupPaths, never, Path.Path>;
  ```
  `configDir = resolveClaudeHomePath(config, environment)`; `accountConfigPath = <configDir>/.claude.json` when `config.homePath.trim()` or `environment?.CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR?.trim()` is non-empty, else `<HostProcess.HomeDirectory>/.claude.json` — exactly the rule ClaudeDriver applies today, because the Claude CLI keeps `.claude.json` beside `~/.claude`, not inside it, when no config dir is set.
- In `claudeLoginFiles.ts`:
  ```ts
  export type JsonObject = { readonly [key: string]: unknown };
  export interface ClaudeSetupLogin {
    readonly claudeAiOauth: JsonObject;  // the whole value under "claudeAiOauth" in .credentials.json, kept verbatim
    readonly oauthAccount: JsonObject;   // the whole value under "oauthAccount" in .claude.json, kept verbatim
    readonly identity: ClaudeAccountIdentity;
  }
  export interface ClaudeAccountIdentity {
    readonly email: string;                     // oauthAccount.emailAddress
    readonly accountUuid: string;               // oauthAccount.accountUuid
    readonly organizationUuid: string | null;   // oauthAccount.organizationUuid, null when absent
  }
  export const sameClaudeAccount: (a: ClaudeAccountIdentity, b: ClaudeAccountIdentity) => boolean; // accountUuid and organizationUuid equal
  export const readClaudeSetupLogin: (
    paths: ClaudeSetupPaths,
  ) => Effect.Effect<Option.Option<ClaudeSetupLogin>, ClaudeLoginFileError, FileSystem.FileSystem>;
  export class ClaudeLoginFileError extends Schema.TaggedError<ClaudeLoginFileError>()("ClaudeLoginFileError", {
    path: Schema.String,
  }) { override get message() { return `Could not read the Claude login file ${this.path}.`; } }
  ```
  `readClaudeSetupLogin` returns `Option.none()` ("not logged in") when `.credentials.json` is missing, has no object `claudeAiOauth`, or that object has no non-empty string `accessToken`; or when `.claude.json` is missing or its `oauthAccount` lacks a non-empty string `emailAddress` or `accountUuid`. It fails with `ClaudeLoginFileError` only when a file exists but cannot be read or is not a JSON object. The error deliberately carries only the path and never the parse cause, because Schema/JSON parse issues can quote the file's content. Values are decoded with `Schema.fromJsonString(Schema.Record(Schema.String, Schema.Unknown))` so every key round-trips unchanged for ticket 2's write-back.
- In `ClaudeAccounts.ts`:
  ```ts
  export type ClaudeAccountErrorReason =
    | "unavailable" | "setupNotFound" | "setupUnreadable" | "notLoggedIn"
    | "invalidName" | "nameInUse" | "alreadyRemembered" | "accountNotFound" | "storage";
  export class ClaudeAccountError extends Schema.TaggedError<ClaudeAccountError>()("ClaudeAccountError", {
    reason: Schema.Literals([...]),
    instanceId: Schema.optional(Schema.String),
    name: Schema.optional(Schema.String),
  }) { override get message(): string { /* per reason, table below */ } }

  export interface RememberedClaudeAccount { readonly name: string; readonly email: string }
  export interface ClaudeSetupAccountState {
    readonly instanceId: ProviderInstanceId;
    readonly displayName: string | undefined;
    readonly active: { readonly email: string; readonly rememberedAs: string | null } | null;
  }
  export interface ClaudeAccountList {
    readonly accounts: ReadonlyArray<RememberedClaudeAccount>;
    readonly setups: ReadonlyArray<ClaudeSetupAccountState>;
  }

  export class ClaudeAccounts extends Context.Service<ClaudeAccounts, {
    readonly remember: (input: { readonly instanceId: ProviderInstanceId; readonly name: string })
      => Effect.Effect<RememberedClaudeAccount, ClaudeAccountError>;
    readonly list: Effect.Effect<ClaudeAccountList, ClaudeAccountError>;
    readonly forget: (input: { readonly name: string }) => Effect.Effect<void, ClaudeAccountError>;
  }>()("t3/provider/ClaudeAccounts") {}
  export const layer: Layer.Layer<ClaudeAccounts, never,
    ServerSecretStore.ServerSecretStore | ServerSettingsService | FileSystem.FileSystem | Path.Path>;
  ```
  Ticket 2 adds `switch` to this same service and reuses its private helpers `resolveSetup(instanceId) → { instanceId, displayName, paths: ClaudeSetupPaths }`, `loadAccounts`, `saveAccounts` and the `accountsLock` semaphore — keep them as named functions inside `make`.

Error messages (`ClaudeAccountError.message`), user-readable and free of login content:
| reason | message |
|---|---|
| `unavailable` | Claude account switching is unavailable on this system. It is supported on Linux only. |
| `setupNotFound` | No Claude setup "<instanceId>" is configured. |
| `setupUnreadable` | Could not read the Claude login of setup "<instanceId>". |
| `notLoggedIn` | No Claude account is logged in on setup "<instanceId>". |
| `invalidName` | An account name must be 1 to 64 characters long. |
| `nameInUse` | The name "<name>" is already in use. |
| `alreadyRemembered` | This account is already remembered as "<name>". |
| `accountNotFound` | No remembered Claude account is named "<name>". |
| `storage` | Could not read or save the remembered Claude accounts. |

Behaviour:
- **Linux gate.** Every method first reads `HostProcess.Platform`; anything but `"linux"` fails with reason `unavailable` before any file or secret is read or written.
- **Setups.** `resolveSetup(instanceId)`: take `deriveProviderInstanceConfigMap(yield* settings.getSettings)`, pick the entry for `instanceId`; missing or `driver !== "claudeAgent"` → `setupNotFound`. Decode `entry.config ?? {}` with `Schema.decodeUnknownEffect(ClaudeSettings)` (a config that fails to decode → `setupUnreadable`), merge `entry.environment` with `mergeProviderInstanceEnvironment`, then `resolveClaudeSetupPaths(config, env)`. `displayName` is `entry.displayName`. `list` uses every entry with `driver === "claudeAgent"`, in map order. Settings read failures map to `storage`.
- **Storage.** One secret named `claude-accounts`, value UTF-8 JSON `{ "version": 1, "accounts": [{ "name": string, "oauthAccount": object, "claudeAiOauth": object }] }`, decoded with a Schema; a missing secret is the empty list. Any `SecretStoreError`, or a stored value that does not decode, fails with reason `storage` and no cause attached (the decode issue would quote the stored login). `remember` and `forget` run their read-modify-write inside `accountsLock` (`Semaphore.make(1)`) and write with `ServerSecretStore.set`, which is atomic and `0o600`.
- **remember.** Gate → `resolveSetup` → `readClaudeSetupLogin(paths)` (`ClaudeLoginFileError` → `setupUnreadable`; `None` → `notLoggedIn`) → under the lock: name is trimmed, 1–64 characters (`invalidName` otherwise); a stored name equal ignoring case → `nameInUse`; a stored record with `sameClaudeAccount` → `alreadyRemembered` with that record's name; else append `{ name, oauthAccount, claudeAiOauth }` and save. Returns `{ name, email }`.
- **list.** Gate → load accounts → for each Claude setup, `readClaudeSetupLogin`; `None` or `ClaudeLoginFileError` → `active: null` (one unreadable setup must not hide the others); otherwise `active.email` from the identity and `rememberedAs` = name of the stored record with `sameClaudeAccount`, else `null`. `accounts` lists `{ name, email: oauthAccount.emailAddress }` in stored order. The result never contains `claudeAiOauth`.
- **forget.** Gate → under the lock: find the record by trimmed name ignoring case (`accountNotFound` otherwise), remove it, save. Never reads or writes any setup file.
- **Logging.** The service logs nothing that contains a record, a file's content or a `claudeAiOauth` value; a failed storage write may log `{ reason }` only.

Decisions:
- One secret holding the whole list, not one secret per account — `remember`/`forget` become one atomic `ServerSecretStore.set`, and listing needs no directory scan of the secrets folder (`ServerSecretStore` has no list method) — gives up per-account files, so the whole list is rewritten on every change (a handful of small records).
- Setup paths come from server settings (`deriveProviderInstanceConfigMap` + `ClaudeSettings`), not from a new service in `ClaudeDriverEnv` — no ripple into the many harnesses that build drivers — gives up reading the live driver's own resolved values; `resolveClaudeSetupPaths` keeps both on one rule so they cannot drift.
- Read the identity from `.claude.json` (`oauthAccount`) instead of the provider snapshot's probed email — no CLI spawn, works for a setup that is not running, and `oauthAccount` is exactly what ticket 2 must swap — gives up nothing the Auftrag needs; the snapshot remains the UI's live source.
- An account is the pair (`accountUuid`, `organizationUuid`), shown by email — one person in two organizations has two different logins — gives up treating them as one account.
- One `ClaudeAccountError` with a `reason` literal, not `ProviderSetupError` — `forget` and `list` have no single `instanceId`, and callers (tests, the later frontend) branch on the reason — gives up reuse of the existing provider setup error.
- Wire `ClaudeAccounts.layer` into `server.ts` now — the service is part of the running server and tickets 2–3 only extend it — gives up nothing; nothing calls it until a transport is added.

Deliberately left out: contracts, WS RPC methods, MCP tools and permission scopes for these actions — the Auftrag says the frontend Auftrag decides how they are triggered; renaming a remembered account; macOS keychain support (unavailable on non-Linux by requirement).
Deliberately added: refusing to remember the same account twice under two names (`alreadyRemembered`) — otherwise "active as <name>" in the list (R2) would be ambiguous; the `resolveClaudeSetupPaths` extraction — the switch in ticket 2 must write exactly the files the driver reads.

Each setup is declared through `ServerSettingsService.layerTest({ providerInstances: { <id>: { driver: "claudeAgent", config: { homePath: <tmp dir> } } } })`, and its login is written by the test as two fixture files: `<tmp>/.credentials.json` = `{ "claudeAiOauth": { "accessToken": "<unique token>", "refreshToken": "<unique token>", "expiresAt": <ms>, "scopes": ["user:inference"] }, "mcpOAuth": { … } }` and `<tmp>/.claude.json` = `{ "oauthAccount": { "emailAddress": "alice@example.com", "accountUuid": "<uuid>", "organizationUuid": "<uuid>" }, "numStartups": 3, "projects": { … } }`. Token fixture values are unique random strings so a leak search cannot match by accident.

Unit (`apps/server/src/provider/Drivers/ClaudeHome.test.ts`, extended):
- `resolveClaudeSetupPaths` with a configured `homePath` returns that directory and `<dir>/.claude.json`.
- With an empty `homePath` and an inherited `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, it returns the inherited directory and `<inherited>/.claude.json`.
- With an empty `homePath` and no inherited `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, it returns `<home>/.claude` and `<home>/.claude.json` (with `HostProcess.HomeDirectory` provided as a temp path; nothing is read from disk).

Integration (`apps/server/src/provider/ClaudeAccounts.integration.test.ts`, through the `ClaudeAccounts` service, real `ServerSecretStore` over `ServerConfig.layerTest(process.cwd(), { prefix: "t3-claude-accounts-test-" })`, real `FileSystem`/`Path`, `HostProcess.Platform` provided as `"linux"` unless stated):
- AK-1: remember `{ instanceId: setupOne, name: "Work" }` on a logged-in setup returns `{ name: "Work", email: "alice@example.com" }`, and `list` then has exactly one account `{ name: "Work", email: "alice@example.com" }`.
- AK-2: after remembering two setups as "Work" and "Private", `list.accounts` is both, in that order.
- AK-3: a setup with no `.credentials.json` (and a second case: `.credentials.json` without `claudeAiOauth`) is refused with `ClaudeAccountError` reason `notLoggedIn`; `list.accounts` is unchanged.
- AK-4: remembering bob's setup as "Work" (and as " work ") is refused with reason `nameInUse`; `list.accounts` still holds exactly `{ name: "Work", email: "alice@example.com" }`.
- Remembering the same account (same `accountUuid` and `organizationUuid`) a second time under another name is refused with reason `alreadyRemembered`, naming the existing name.
- AK-5: two setups, two remembered accounts: `list.setups` shows setup one `active: { email: "alice@example.com", rememberedAs: "Work" }` and setup two `active: { email: "bob@example.com", rememberedAs: "Private" }`.
- AK-6: a setup with carol logged in and nothing remembered for carol shows `active: { email: "carol@example.com", rememberedAs: null }`.
- AK-7: with nothing remembered, `list.accounts` is `[]` and every configured Claude setup is still listed with its active account; a setup with nobody logged in is listed with `active: null`; a non-Claude instance (e.g. `driver: "codex"`) is not listed.
- AK-8: forget "Private" leaves `list.accounts` = `[Work]`.
- AK-9: forget "Work" while alice is logged in on setup one: `list.accounts` is `[]`, and both `<tmp>/.credentials.json` and `<tmp>/.claude.json` are byte-identical to before the call; `list.setups` still shows alice active with `rememberedAs: null`.
- Forgetting a name that is not remembered is refused with reason `accountNotFound`.
- AK-23: after remember, the secret `claude-accounts` exists in `<stateDir>/secrets/claude-accounts.bin` with file mode `0o600` in a `0o700` directory (same as every other T3 secret); a recursive walk of the whole temporary T3 base directory finds the fixture access token and refresh token in no file other than `claude-accounts.bin`.
- AK-24: `JSON.stringify(list)` contains neither fixture token, nor the substrings `accessToken`, `refreshToken`, `claudeAiOauth`; the listed account objects have exactly the keys `name` and `email`.
- No error raised by the service carries login content: for every refusal above, `JSON.stringify(error)` and `error.message` contain no fixture token.
- AK-27/AK-28/AK-29: with `HostProcess.Platform` provided as `"darwin"` (and once as `"win32"`), `remember`, `list` and `forget` each fail with reason `unavailable` and message "Claude account switching is unavailable on this system. It is supported on Linux only."; after the failed `remember`, `<stateDir>/secrets/claude-accounts.bin` does not exist.
Boundaries doubled: `HostProcess.Platform` and `HostProcess.HomeDirectory` (host OS), and the setup files (fixture files in temp dirs standing in for what the Claude CLI writes); everything else real — `ServerSecretStore`, `ServerSettingsService.layerTest`, `FileSystem`, `Path`.
e2e:
- There is no e2e suite (guard rail). AK-9's last line ("a new turn … runs as alice@example.com") needs a real Claude CLI; it is proven at the lowest level that can prove it: the setup's two login files are byte-identical after forgetting, so the next turn reads the same login. Named as such in the hand-off.

### Implementation details
Module: `apps/server` (provider)
Files:
- [MODIFY] `apps/server/src/provider/Drivers/ClaudeHome.ts` — add `resolveClaudeSetupPaths`, the one place that knows where a setup keeps its login and its account file.
- [MODIFY] `apps/server/src/provider/Drivers/ClaudeHome.test.ts` — unit tests for `resolveClaudeSetupPaths`.
- [MODIFY] `apps/server/src/provider/Drivers/ClaudeDriver.ts` — replace the inline `configDir`/`accountConfigPath` computation (lines 158–163) with `resolveClaudeSetupPaths(effectiveConfig, processEnv)`; behaviour unchanged.
- [MODIFY] `apps/server/src/provider/claudeResetCredits.ts` — delete the `claudeAccountConfigPath` export, whose only importer was ClaudeDriver (Knip fails CI on an unused export).
- [NEW] `apps/server/src/provider/claudeLoginFiles.ts` — read a setup's current Claude login and account identity from its two files.
- [NEW] `apps/server/src/provider/ClaudeAccounts.ts` — the `ClaudeAccounts` service: remember, list, forget, Linux gate, storage in `ServerSecretStore`.
- [NEW] `apps/server/src/provider/ClaudeAccounts.integration.test.ts` — the integration tests above.
- [MODIFY] `apps/server/src/server.ts` — add `ClaudeAccounts.layer` to the `Layer.mergeAll(...)` list of `layerRuntimeCoreDependenciesBase` next to `ProviderUsageLimitsIngestion.layer` (server.ts:601), where `layerServerSettings` and `ServerSecretStore.layer` are provided below it.

Consumes: nothing from earlier tickets. Existing: `ServerSecretStore.ServerSecretStore` (`get`, `set`), `ServerSettingsService` (`getSettings`), `deriveProviderInstanceConfigMap` (ProviderInstanceRegistryHydration.ts), `ClaudeSettings` (`@t3tools/contracts`), `mergeProviderInstanceEnvironment` (`@t3tools/provider-core/server/instanceEnvironment`), `resolveClaudeHomePath`, `HostProcess.Platform`, `HostProcess.HomeDirectory`.

Produces (names used letter for letter by tickets 2 and 3):
- In `ClaudeHome.ts`:
  ```ts
  export interface ClaudeSetupPaths {
    readonly configDir: string;          // holds .credentials.json
    readonly accountConfigPath: string;  // the .claude.json holding oauthAccount
  }
  export const resolveClaudeSetupPaths: (
    config: Pick<ClaudeSettings, "homePath">,
    environment?: NodeJS.ProcessEnv,
  ) => Effect.Effect<ClaudeSetupPaths, never, Path.Path>;
  ```
  `configDir = resolveClaudeHomePath(config, environment)`; `accountConfigPath = <configDir>/.claude.json` when `config.homePath.trim()` or `environment?.CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR?.trim()` is non-empty, else `<HostProcess.HomeDirectory>/.claude.json` — exactly the rule ClaudeDriver applies today, because the Claude CLI keeps `.claude.json` beside `~/.claude`, not inside it, when no config dir is set.
- In `claudeLoginFiles.ts`:
  ```ts
  export type JsonObject = { readonly [key: string]: unknown };
  export interface ClaudeSetupLogin {
    readonly claudeAiOauth: JsonObject;  // the whole value under "claudeAiOauth" in .credentials.json, kept verbatim
    readonly oauthAccount: JsonObject;   // the whole value under "oauthAccount" in .claude.json, kept verbatim
    readonly identity: ClaudeAccountIdentity;
  }
  export interface ClaudeAccountIdentity {
    readonly email: string;                     // oauthAccount.emailAddress
    readonly accountUuid: string;               // oauthAccount.accountUuid
    readonly organizationUuid: string | null;   // oauthAccount.organizationUuid, null when absent
  }
  export const sameClaudeAccount: (a: ClaudeAccountIdentity, b: ClaudeAccountIdentity) => boolean; // accountUuid and organizationUuid equal
  export const readClaudeSetupLogin: (
    paths: ClaudeSetupPaths,
  ) => Effect.Effect<Option.Option<ClaudeSetupLogin>, ClaudeLoginFileError, FileSystem.FileSystem>;
  export class ClaudeLoginFileError extends Schema.TaggedError<ClaudeLoginFileError>()("ClaudeLoginFileError", {
    path: Schema.String,
  }) { override get message() { return `Could not read the Claude login file ${this.path}.`; } }
  ```
  `readClaudeSetupLogin` returns `Option.none()` ("not logged in") when `.credentials.json` is missing, has no object `claudeAiOauth`, or that object has no non-empty string `accessToken`; or when `.claude.json` is missing or its `oauthAccount` lacks a non-empty string `emailAddress` or `accountUuid`. It fails with `ClaudeLoginFileError` only when a file exists but cannot be read or is not a JSON object. The error deliberately carries only the path and never the parse cause, because Schema/JSON parse issues can quote the file's content. Values are decoded with `Schema.fromJsonString(Schema.Record(Schema.String, Schema.Unknown))` so every key round-trips unchanged for ticket 2's write-back.
- In `ClaudeAccounts.ts`:
  ```ts
  export type ClaudeAccountErrorReason =
    | "unavailable" | "setupNotFound" | "setupUnreadable" | "notLoggedIn"
    | "invalidName" | "nameInUse" | "alreadyRemembered" | "accountNotFound" | "storage";
  export class ClaudeAccountError extends Schema.TaggedError<ClaudeAccountError>()("ClaudeAccountError", {
    reason: Schema.Literals(["unavailable", "setupNotFound", "setupUnreadable", "notLoggedIn", "invalidName", "nameInUse", "alreadyRemembered", "accountNotFound", "storage"]),
    instanceId: Schema.optional(Schema.String),
    name: Schema.optional(Schema.String),
  }) { override get message(): string { /* the message for this.reason from the table below */ } }

  export interface RememberedClaudeAccount { readonly name: string; readonly email: string }
  export interface ClaudeSetupAccountState {
    readonly instanceId: ProviderInstanceId;
    readonly displayName: string | undefined;
    readonly active: { readonly email: string; readonly rememberedAs: string | null } | null;
  }
  export interface ClaudeAccountList {
    readonly accounts: ReadonlyArray<RememberedClaudeAccount>;
    readonly setups: ReadonlyArray<ClaudeSetupAccountState>;
  }

  export class ClaudeAccounts extends Context.Service<ClaudeAccounts, {
    readonly remember: (input: { readonly instanceId: ProviderInstanceId; readonly name: string })
      => Effect.Effect<RememberedClaudeAccount, ClaudeAccountError>;
    readonly list: Effect.Effect<ClaudeAccountList, ClaudeAccountError>;
    readonly forget: (input: { readonly name: string }) => Effect.Effect<void, ClaudeAccountError>;
  }>()("t3/provider/ClaudeAccounts") {}
  export const layer: Layer.Layer<ClaudeAccounts, never,
    ServerSecretStore.ServerSecretStore | ServerSettingsService | FileSystem.FileSystem | Path.Path>;
  ```
  Ticket 2 adds `switch` to this same service and reuses its private helpers `resolveSetup(instanceId) → { instanceId, displayName, paths: ClaudeSetupPaths }`, `loadAccounts`, `saveAccounts` and the `accountsLock` semaphore — keep them as named functions inside `make`.

Error messages (`ClaudeAccountError.message`), user-readable and free of login content:
| reason | message |
|---|---|
| `unavailable` | Claude account switching is unavailable on this system. It is supported on Linux only. |
| `setupNotFound` | No Claude setup "<instanceId>" is configured. |
| `setupUnreadable` | Could not read the Claude login of setup "<instanceId>". |
| `notLoggedIn` | No Claude account is logged in on setup "<instanceId>". |
| `invalidName` | An account name must be 1 to 64 characters long. |
| `nameInUse` | The name "<name>" is already in use. |
| `alreadyRemembered` | This account is already remembered as "<name>". |
| `accountNotFound` | No remembered Claude account is named "<name>". |
| `storage` | Could not read or save the remembered Claude accounts. |

Behaviour:
- **Linux gate.** Every method first reads `HostProcess.Platform`; anything but `"linux"` fails with reason `unavailable` before any file or secret is read or written.
- **Setups.** `resolveSetup(instanceId)`: take `deriveProviderInstanceConfigMap(yield* settings.getSettings)`, pick the entry for `instanceId`; missing or `driver !== "claudeAgent"` → `setupNotFound`. Decode `entry.config ?? {}` with `Schema.decodeUnknownEffect(ClaudeSettings)` (a config that fails to decode → `setupUnreadable`), merge `entry.environment` with `mergeProviderInstanceEnvironment`, then `resolveClaudeSetupPaths(config, env)`. `displayName` is `entry.displayName`. `list` uses every entry with `driver === "claudeAgent"`, in map order. Settings read failures map to `storage`.
- **Storage.** One secret named `claude-accounts`, value UTF-8 JSON `{ "version": 1, "accounts": [{ "name": string, "oauthAccount": object, "claudeAiOauth": object }] }`, decoded with a Schema; a missing secret is the empty list. Any `SecretStoreError`, or a stored value that does not decode, fails with reason `storage` and no cause attached (the decode issue would quote the stored login). `remember` and `forget` run their read-modify-write inside `accountsLock` (`Semaphore.make(1)`) and write with `ServerSecretStore.set`, which is atomic and `0o600`.
- **remember.** Gate → `resolveSetup` → `readClaudeSetupLogin(paths)` (`ClaudeLoginFileError` → `setupUnreadable`; `None` → `notLoggedIn`) → under the lock: name is trimmed, 1–64 characters (`invalidName` otherwise); a stored name equal ignoring case → `nameInUse`; a stored record with `sameClaudeAccount` → `alreadyRemembered` with that record's name; else append `{ name, oauthAccount, claudeAiOauth }` and save. Returns `{ name, email }`.
- **list.** Gate → load accounts → for each Claude setup, `readClaudeSetupLogin`; `None` or `ClaudeLoginFileError` → `active: null` (one unreadable setup must not hide the others); otherwise `active.email` from the identity and `rememberedAs` = name of the stored record with `sameClaudeAccount`, else `null`. `accounts` lists `{ name, email: oauthAccount.emailAddress }` in stored order. The result never contains `claudeAiOauth`.
- **forget.** Gate → under the lock: find the record by trimmed name ignoring case (`accountNotFound` otherwise), remove it, save. Never reads or writes any setup file.
- **Logging.** The service logs nothing that contains a record, a file's content or a `claudeAiOauth` value; a failed storage write may log `{ reason }` only.

Decisions:
- One secret holding the whole list, not one secret per account — `remember`/`forget` become one atomic `ServerSecretStore.set`, and listing needs no directory scan of the secrets folder (`ServerSecretStore` has no list method) — gives up per-account files, so the whole list is rewritten on every change (a handful of small records).
- Setup paths come from server settings (`deriveProviderInstanceConfigMap` + `ClaudeSettings`), not from a new service in `ClaudeDriverEnv` — no ripple into the many harnesses that build drivers — gives up reading the live driver's own resolved values; `resolveClaudeSetupPaths` keeps both on one rule so they cannot drift.
- Read the identity from `.claude.json` (`oauthAccount`) instead of the provider snapshot's probed email — no CLI spawn, works for a setup that is not running, and `oauthAccount` is exactly what ticket 2 must swap — gives up nothing the Auftrag needs; the snapshot remains the UI's live source.
- An account is the pair (`accountUuid`, `organizationUuid`), shown by email — one person in two organizations has two different logins — gives up treating them as one account.
- One `ClaudeAccountError` with a `reason` literal, not `ProviderSetupError` — `forget` and `list` have no single `instanceId`, and callers (tests, the later frontend) branch on the reason — gives up reuse of the existing provider setup error.
- Wire `ClaudeAccounts.layer` into `server.ts` now — the service is part of the running server and tickets 2–3 only extend it — gives up nothing; nothing calls it until a transport is added.

Deliberately left out: contracts, WS RPC methods, MCP tools and permission scopes for these actions — the Auftrag says the frontend Auftrag decides how they are triggered; renaming a remembered account; macOS keychain support (unavailable on non-Linux by requirement).
Deliberately added: refusing to remember the same account twice under two names (`alreadyRemembered`) — otherwise "active as <name>" in the list (R2) would be ambiguous; the `resolveClaudeSetupPaths` extraction — the switch in ticket 2 must write exactly the files the driver reads.
